text:
maya: Heads-up — canary for raven-lite-v3 (int4) is showing funcall parse failures only on streaming + kv_prefix enabled. low volume but reproducible.

maya: sample run id rnl-2026-03-20-01, triggered from canary job. Non-streaming responses look ok. Streaming ones sometimes emit interleaved human text between JSON fragments which breaks the parser.

todd: Do we have an example stream sequence?

maya: pasted a minimal reproduction below (stream chunks in order received):
```
[chunk 1] {"id":1,"type":"tool_call","name":"get_profile","args":
[chunk 2] \"{\"user_id\":123}\"
Some followup text: thanks!
[chunk 3] }
```

maya: Parser errors because 'Some followup text' appears before the closing brace. If you reassemble naively based on arrival order it becomes invalid JSON.

rav: I've seen this pattern on an int8 canary earlier but much rarer. My suspicion: KV prefix cache + streaming batching can trigger token emission reordering or extra system text tokens getting emitted between arg tokens. Could also be a tokenizer boundary issue.

lin: Can runtime reorder chunks? We normally assign sequence ids but the canary traces don't include them today. If runtime sends chunks out-of-order due to batching, the client should reorder by seq. Do we have sequence metadata in the stream events?

maya: not in the canary trace logs we capture. The streaming client just receives a flat stream.

ci-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary: raven-lite-v3-int4 rolled to 10% at 02:12 UTC. Metrics: funcall_parse_rate=2.1% (baseline 0.1%).

eva: :thinking_face: We currently have a soft-rescue in the agent that tries a regex-based repair or retries the model with "return only JSON" — that reduces customer-facing errors but masks the underlying issue.

rav: Proposal (short term): add chunk sequence_id to stream events in traces and log kv_prefix_applied flag per request. Long term: identify whether compiler optimizations (prefix_rewrite) or runtime batching cause emission order change.

lin: quick patch idea: have runtime emit a small header in each stream event: {chunk_seq: N, kv_prefix_applied: true|false}. That will let us correlate arrival order vs seq. I'll PR today.

maya: Experiments I want to run tonight: four buckets A/B/C/D (5k samples each)
- A: int4, streaming, kv_prefix=on
- B: int4, streaming, kv_prefix=off
- C: int8, streaming, kv_prefix=on
- D: int8, streaming, kv_prefix=off
Measure: funcall_parse_rate, avg latency, and % with reordering (seq mismatch).

todd: Also run a compiler-disabled bucket where prefix_rewrite is turned off. That optimization has bitten us before.

rav: Add to the capture: raw token ids around the toolcall region for failed samples. Helps us see whether tokenization boundaries are the culprit.

maya: quick repro note: turning kv_prefix off seems to make failures vanish in a small local sample. That points at prefix handling.

ops: If canary funcall_parse_rate > 1% on Dedicated we should roll raven-lite-v3-int4 back to 0% — ops can execute rollback.

ci-bot: [ci] job rnl-eval-2801456 started, harness: toolcall-stress-5k.

lin: small instrumentation follow-up: we should emit an explicit sentinel token wrapper for tool calls in streaming mode, e.g., <TOOL_START> ... <TOOL_END>. That way intermediate human text can't be mistaken for part of the JSON. We'll try sentinel as an experiment if seq metadata shows reorder.

eva: Fallback options: 1) keep soft-rescue (retries with "only JSON" prompt) to reduce user impact; 2) block canary promotion until root cause found; 3) add sentinel patch and re-run. Note that retries add cost + latency.

todd: Agreed we shouldn't ship heuristics as permanent fix. Use them as mitigating ops while we hunt root cause.

rav: Action items:
- Lin: add chunk_seq + kv_prefix flag to streaming traces (today)
- Maya: run the 4-bucket canary (tonight) and post CSV of failures
- Rav: collect raw token id dumps for all failed samples and run tokenizer-alignment check
- Eva: prepare eval harness change to include retry-cost accounting
- Ops: ready rollback plan if rate > 1%

maya: Will post results in this thread. Thanks folks. :pray:
